==English==

===Etymology 1===
This surname has multiple origins. Besides the ones listed below, Norman origin has also been suggested from De Haie",<ref>Elisabeth Alice Gibbens Cole, ''An Account of Our Day Family of Calvert County, Maryland'' (1940), p. 49.</ref> or "a corruption of the Normandy French D'Ossone, from the town of Ossone, in Normandy". <ref>[http://www.searchforancestors.com/surnames/origin/d/day.php Day Surname Origin & Last Name Meaning] at Ancestor Search.</ref>

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/deɪ/}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪ|s=1}}
* {{hmp|en|day|dey|Dey}}

====Proper noun====
{{en-proper noun}}
{{wp|<dab!>}}

# {{surname|en|from=patronymics}} derived from a medieval diminutive of [[David]].<ref>[http://www.searchforancestors.com/surnames/origin/d/day.php Day Surname Origin & Last Name Meaning] at Ancestor Search.</ref>
# {{surname|en|English|from=occupations}} from [[day]] as a word for a "day-servant", an archaic term for a [[day-laborer]],<ref>Ernest Weekley, ''The Romance of Words'' (1927), p. 165.</ref> or from given names such as Dagr, Daug, Dege, and Dey, cognate with Scandinavian [[Dag]].<ref>Susa Young Gates, ''Surname Book and Racial History'' (1918) p. 289.</ref>
# {{surname|en|from=Irish}} can be found as both Day and [[O'Day]] from {{m|ga|Ó Deághaidh||descendant of a person named Good Luck}}.

===Etymology===
* As an English surname, from the noun {{m|en|money}}. Compare {{m|en|Minter}}, {{m|en|Monier}}.
* As an {{der|en|ga|-}} surname, variant of {{m|en|Mooney}}.
* As a {{der|en|fr|-}} surname, variant of {{m|en|Monnet}}, itself a variant of {{m|en|Monet}}.

===Proper noun===
{{en-proper noun|~|s}}

# {{surname|en}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1991|author=Eli Coleman|title=John Money: A Tribute|page=xiv
|passage=This point highlights several of John '''Money''''s contributions to the field of behavioral science.}}
# {{place|en|ucomm|co/Leflore County|s/Mississippi|c/USA}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2021|author={{w|Percival Everett}}|title=[[w:The Trees (Everett novel)|The Trees]]|publisher=Influx Press (2022)|page=11|passage='''Money''', Mississippi, looks exactly like it sounds. Named in that persistent Southern tradition of irony and with the attendant tradition of nescience, the name becomes slightly sad, a marker of self-conscious ignorance that might as well be embraced because, let’s face it, it isn’t going away.}}
# {{place|en|ucomm|co/Gloucester County|s/Virginia|c/USA}}.

====Statistics====
* According to the 2010 United States Census, ''Money'' is the 5421<sup>st</sup> most common surname in the United States, belonging to 6420 individuals. ''Money'' is most common among White (84.78%) individuals.
